newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent trades lower as NYMEX tests support.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent trades lower as NYMEX tests support.

text.p: Brent crude futures were lower on Tuesday, falling in line with a correction on NYMEX as longs cut positions.
July Brent was last traded at $19.85 per barrel, down 15 cents from London's settlement on Friday.
Brokers said NYMEX was testing support on the July contract around $21.45, prompting some nervous longs to lighten their positions on both sides of the Atlantic.
"A break below $21.40 would cause some further selling," a broker said.

July NYMEX crude, which fell 23 cents to $21.63 in New York, was last traded on the after-hours ACCESS system at $21.49 -- a further loss of 14 cents. However, the contract traded as low as $21.39 as the support was tested.
Brokers said short term direction was in the hands of the U.S. gasoline market, as polayers waited for the start of the summer driving season in the U.S..
NYMEX and IPE were both closed on Monday due to public holidays.
